A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LOB-Bench study. Their complete text, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GOOG and INTC experiments, including distributional comparisons, discriminator performance, impact response curves and model training results.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds downstream mid-price prediction experiments and a bin-size sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 extends the evaluation framework with an MLP-based utility procedure comparing predictors trained on real-only and augmented data. This adds a benchmark component; the generative architectures, training objectives and inference procedures are retained.

E1.justification: v2 adds supervised three-class mid-price forecasting to test the usefulness of synthetic GOOG training data. This substantially extends task coverage beyond distributional realism and market-response matching. The existing GOOG/INTC market coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new forecasting comparison introduces real-data-only MLP reference models against predictors trained with additional synthetic data. Figure 8 evaluates LOBS5, the Cont baseline and Coletta. Comparator membership in the retained generative comparisons is unchanged, including RWKV-4 and RWKV-6.

E3.justification: The new forecasting protocol uses a million-parameter MLP, three movement classes, real-only versus augmented training, held-out real-data F1 scores and five prediction horizons. Appendix D adds half-width and double-width histogram settings. Existing generative training budgets and data periods are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix D tests sensitivity of LOBS5 divergence scores to halving and doubling the Freedman–Diaconis bin width. Figure 11 adds a focused robustness check absent from v1; the earlier error-accumulation and conditional-distribution analyses remain.

E5.justification: Figure 8 newly reports 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from five MLP training seeds. The earlier 99% confidence intervals and real-data bootstrap thresholds are retained. This documents repeated training for the new task, rather than an increase in runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial downstream utility evidence: Figure 8 shows markedly lower F1 with Coletta-generated augmentation and little long-horizon change for LOBS5 and the Cont baseline. Figure 11 adds systematic bin-width effects on divergence scores. Existing headline results, including impact distances of 2.45 for LOBS5 and 126 for RWKV-6, are retained.

T1.justification: Section 4 revises the formal horizon-divergence expression: v1 conditions both distributions on the forecasting interval, whereas v2 leaves the real-data reference unconditional. This aligns the formula with the introduction's existing description; it does not establish that experiments were rerun.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about distributional benchmarking, LOBS5's superior realism, error accumulation and extensibility. The added experiments do not redefine the principal claimed contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a practical limitation: synthetic data does not improve the tested forecasting task, which also provides limited differentiation between generators. It adds explanations of discriminator separability and bin-size effects. Its new assertion of stable cross-model rankings exceeds the LOBS5-only sensitivity evidence shown.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 identifies the LOBCAST implementation and million-parameter MLP used for the new experiment. Appendix A adds a project website for additional resources alongside the existing repository. The detailed LOBS5 and RWKV training disclosures remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Goodfellow et al. (2014) and Prata et al. (2024), with LOBCAST supporting the new forecasting evaluation. The main research positioning remains stable. Updates to Sennrich and LeCun/Bengio concern works already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose corrections and explanatory expansions, updates affiliations, and adds Section 4.3, the sensitivity appendix and a generic Impact Statement. The overall narrative and main section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds forecasting Figure 8 and sensitivity Figure 11, expands and emphasizes captions, and relocates existing figures. The divergence panels, v1 Figure 16 and v2 Figure 18, receive cleaner title and legend spacing. Most existing graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: The five-seed forecasting experiment adds useful evidence about practical utility beyond v1's realism assessments, and the bin-size study supplies a focused robustness check. These improve the paper while preserving its original evidence. The gains are limited by unspecified forecasting details, including the class threshold and data mixing ratio, and by the unsupported extrapolation from a LOBS5-only ablation to cross-model ranking stability.
